headline: intg-prod-a1: cause not established — convergence blocked pending audit log and setroubleshootd log; setroubleshootd at 99.7% CPU since 2026-03-02 correlates with batch latency and console slowness; five blocking evidence items outstanding

SELinux is confirmed in enforcing mode; denials are real and being logged.
Integration service JVM (pid 3489339) is at 5.6% CPU and 24.8 GiB resident set at snapshot time.
Memory exhaustion problems P-4100 through P-4112 — 13 problems in total — all opened in the 03:00–04:00 UTC window and auto-closed approximately 2.5 hours later over a 15-day span.
All 13 problems were unacknowledged, unassigned, and unactioned; the observability platform note states no problem in this window was acknowledged, assigned or actioned.
Memory series shows a rising sawtooth pattern beginning 2026-03-02T00:00:00+00:00.

The audit-analysis-server package has been installed on this host for 3 years; the 2026-03-02T06:00:00+00:00 timestamp is an activation event, not an installation event.
No heap or thread dump has been collected from the JVM (pid 3489339).
No pipeline deployments are recorded for intg-prod-a1; any application-layer change delivered outside the pipeline is invisible to the change registry.
The non-production equivalent host (intg-nonprod-a1) has build_parity=false with a different patch level and different installed agents.
standing_conditions: Integration service JVM on intg-prod-a1 holds 23.1 GiB resident of 32 GiB total RAM as steady state for at least 6 months, with no alerting configured and no owner assigned. This leaves only approximately 8.9 GiB free at baseline, meaning any additional persistent process such as setroubleshootd at 622 MB materially reduces the margin before memory exhaustion. This condition did not cause the incident but explains why a new consumer was able to trigger exhaustion.

13 memory exhaustion problems (P-4100 through P-4112) fired and auto-closed over 15 days with zero acknowledgements, zero assignments, and zero actions taken. The auto-close behaviour created a false impression of self-resolution and allowed a progressive degradation to reach user-visible impact undetected. Alerting configuration and on-call response procedures for auto-closing problems on this host require review as a post-incident finding.

The change registry has a confirmed blind spot: self_updating_agents_not_reflected=true. Agents that self-update do not produce package records, meaning the current running version of any self-updating agent on this host may differ from the registry without any audit trail. This is a standing gap in change visibility for this host.
No pipeline deployments are recorded for intg-prod-a1; any application-layer change delivered outside the pipeline is invisible to the change registry. This is a standing gap in change traceability.

intg-nonprod-a1 has build_parity=false with a different patch level and different installed agents; it cannot be used to safely reproduce or test hypotheses about production behaviour without accounting for these differences.
suspected: SUPPORTED — setroubleshootd is consuming approximately 100% CPU in response to a high-volume stream of SELinux AVC denials that began 2026-03-02, and this CPU saturation is the proximate cause of batch transfer latency and console slowness on intg-prod-a1. Supporting: process snapshot directly observes setroubleshootd at 99.7% CPU on an 8-core host, leaving approximately 0.3 cores for all other processes; SELinux is in enforcing mode and setroubleshootd activates in response to denial volume; JVM at 5.6% CPU makes it an unlikely direct cause of saturation; the memory sawtooth onset coincides with setroubleshootd activation and is consistent with a nightly batch workload driving resources to exhaustion. Contradicting: no direct observation of AVC denial volume or rate exists; the audit log is outstanding; the link between setroubleshootd CPU consumption and a denial storm is inferential. Falsifying test: inspect /var/log/audit/audit.log for AVC denial counts per hour from 2026-03-02 onward — if denial volume is low or absent, setroubleshootd CPU consumption has a different cause not yet identified.

PLAUSIBLE — CHG-88104 (endpoint-compliance-agent 7.4.2-27, installed 2026-02-22) triggered novel SELinux AVC denials that activated setroubleshootd on 2026-03-02, initiating the CPU and memory exhaustion pattern. Supporting: CHG-88104 is the only change record in the pre-onset window per the change correlator (confidence: plausible); the registry caveat self_updating_agents_not_reflected=true means the agent may have self-updated between 2026-02-22 and 2026-03-02, which could be consistent with the 8-day gap between installation and onset; setroubleshootd activation at 2026-03-02T06:00:00+00:00 coincides with close of P-4100; SELinux enforcing mode confirmed. Contradicting: the 8-day gap between agent installation and onset weakens temporal proximity; no AVC denial log yet collected to confirm the agent is the source domain; self_updating_agents_not_reflected=true means the version running at onset may differ from 7.4.2-27 with no registry evidence. Note: this hypothesis cites a prior incident pattern; the divergence is that the current incident has no recorded heap configuration change, unlike INC-2411. Falsifying test: inspect /var/log/audit/audit.log for AVC denials from 2026-02-22 through 2026-03-02 — if no denials are attributable to the endpoint-compliance-agent source domain, this hypothesis is falsified; additionally confirm whether the agent was active and consuming memory between 2026-02-22 and 2026-03-01, as flat memory during that period weakens the correlation.

PLAUSIBLE — the integration service JVM has a memory leak contributing to the rising sawtooth memory pattern, with the JVM resident set growing during each batch cycle and partially recovering, compounding memory exhaustion alongside setroubleshootd. Supporting: memory series shows a rising sawtooth with climbs of approximately 3.5 GiB over approximately 15 hours then sharp drops repeating each cycle from 2026-03-02; JVM resident set at 24.8 GiB is elevated above the 23.1 GiB steady-state baseline noted for 6 months; this hypothesis cites prior incident INC-2411 (memory exhaustion on an integration-class host with a JVM workload) — divergence noted: INC-2411 had a recorded heap configuration change, which is absent here. Contradicting: JVM CPU is only 5.6%, inconsistent with a runaway workload driving memory growth; the sharp sawtooth drop is more consistent with a process restart or GC event than a leak, which would typically not recover without intervention; the 24.8 GiB reading is elevated above the 23.1 GiB baseline but not dramatically so. Falsifying test: collect a JVM heap dump from pid 3489339 — if heap occupancy is stable and within historical norms, the JVM is not contributing to the memory growth pattern; swap metrics would also clarify whether the JVM is being paged out during exhaustion events.

SUPPORTED — recurring nightly memory exhaustion events P-4100 through P-4112 have been auto-closing without acknowledgement for 15 days, masking a progressive degradation that has now manifested as user-visible latency. Supporting: all 13 problems are unacknowledged per direct observation; problems auto-close after approximately 2.5 hours each night, creating a false impression of self-resolution; user-reported batch latency and console slowness are consistent with the host operating near memory and CPU exhaustion during batch windows; this cites prior incident INC-2419 (same signature, same auto-close behaviour, ran 10 days unacknowledged before action) — divergence noted: INC-2419 was resolved by restart without establishing cause, and that outcome must not be repeated here. Contradicting: auto-close could reflect genuine recovery if the batch workload completes and memory is released; the pattern alone does not confirm suppression of a worsening condition. Falsifying test: compare batch transfer completion times and console response times on days when problems were open versus closed — if performance is identical in both states, the auto-closing events are not causing user-visible impact.
